title: Pan-Seared Fillet Steak
summary: A pan-seared fillet steak for one. It cooks faster than ribeye, even though you take it further, because it is leaner with less fat to render.

steps.text: Take the steak out of the fridge {timer:30} before cooking. Pat it completely dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with the butter. Fillet is leaner and cooks faster, so a medium heat stops the outside burning before the inside is cooked.
Once the butter foams, add the steak. Sear for about {timer:4} per side for a 200 g fillet cooked to medium.
Add the thyme, rosemary and garlic, if using, and baste the steak with the butter as it cooks, using a spoon.
Move to a plate and rest for {timer:5}. The internal temperature should be {temp:57-60!} for medium.

tips: Fillet has less marbling than ribeye, so use butter throughout cooking. A medium heat is crucial. For accuracy, use a meat thermometer: 52-55 °C for medium-rare, 57-60 °C for medium, 63-66 °C for medium-well. If you want to change the weight of the fillet, you can ask the AI assistant to adjust the cooking times and temperatures.
